title: Credit Balance and Refund Policy, Patient Invoices & Statements
content:
A credit balance on a Patient Invoices & Statements invoice is a balance due below zero: an amount the laboratory owes the patient on that invoice.

## Policy

**1. How a credit balance arises.** A credit balance arises from an overpayment, from a payment followed by an adjustment, or from an insurance payment received after the patient paid.

**2. Credits below the refund threshold.** A credit balance below the billing class's refund threshold is held on the invoice.

**3. Credits at or above the refund threshold.** Where the billing class's setting for transferring a credit first to the patient's other open invoices is Yes, a credit at or above the refund threshold is first transferred to the patient's other invoices whose status is open, oldest date of service first, each up to its balance due, and only the remainder is refunded to the original payment method.

**4. Invoices that never receive a transfer.** A credit is never transferred to an invoice in collections, on hold or on a payment plan.

**5. Refund timing.** Refunds are issued within the billing class's refund time, in calendar days, of the credit arising. A consumer purchase refunded after an order cancellation follows the refund timing of Laboratory Test Orders instead.

**6. How a disbursement shows on the invoices.** A refund shows on the invoice that held the credit as a refund to the original payment method. A transfer shows on that invoice as a refund transferred to an open invoice, naming the invoice that receives it, and on the receiving invoice as a payment by credit balance transfer through internal transfer, for the same amount.

## Worked allocation (hypothetical patient, class whose transfer setting is Yes)

Invoice S carries a credit balance of 90.00, at or above the refund threshold. The patient's other invoices are:

| Invoice | Status | Date of service | Balance due | Credit received |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| K | Open | 5 January 2026 | 45.00 | 45.00 |
| Y | Open | 10 February 2026 | 30.00 | 30.00 |
| Z | Payment plan | 2 December 2025 | 200.00 | none |
| Q | Collections | 14 November 2025 | 75.00 | none |

K has the oldest date of service among the open invoices and receives up to its balance due, 45.00; Y then receives up to its balance due, 30.00. Z and Q receive nothing even though their dates of service are older, because a credit is never transferred to an invoice on a payment plan or in collections. The remainder, 90.00 less 45.00 less 30.00, is 15.00, refunded to the original payment method.

Had the credit on S been 40.00 instead, K alone would have received 40.00, leaving 5.00 due on K, and nothing would remain to refund.

A credit on S smaller than the class's refund threshold is neither transferred nor refunded; it stays on S.
